transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Since I stopped working, I’m struggling with how to handle this change, and my reactions are keeping me from settling into a new routine. It has just been a lot more disorienting to transition into retirement than I ever expected it to be.
When did these difficulties adjusting to retirement begin, and did they start within about three months of stopping work?

The first few weeks after leaving my engineering firm were actually fine, but by about two months into retirement, I started feeling oddly stuck and uneasy. That's when this unsettled feeling really set in, and I began avoiding the activities I had planned to enjoy.

How much is this affecting your day-to-day life—for example, your relationships, self-care, or ability to manage your usual responsibilities? Is it causing more distress or impairment than you would expect for a normal adjustment to retirement?

It is causing more disruption than I expected, to the point where my wife has noticed me declining social invitations and postponing trips we'd planned, like visiting Yosemite or Oaxaca. I often feel paralyzed by simple daily choices, ending up pacing around or reorganizing old engineering files instead of hiking or gardening. This has thinned out our social calendar and leaves me feeling quite unsettled and disappointed in myself.

Around the time these symptoms began, was retirement the main stressor, or were there any other major losses or events—such as a death, serious illness, or financial problem—that might also be contributing?

Retirement was definitely the main transition, and fortunately, we don't have any financial worries or major losses like a death in the family. However, the transition became much harder when the local STEM program I planned to volunteer with paused, and several of my close hiking partners either moved away or developed health issues. Those changes really eroded the social and active routines I had lined up, making me feel even more unmoored.

Since this started, have you had persistent depression or loss of interest most of the day nearly every day, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living? I also want to ask whether you’ve had intense anxiety or panic attacks that seem out of proportion to the retirement transition.

No, I haven't experienced persistent depression, thoughts like that, or any intense panic attacks. My difficulties are really limited to feeling unsettled, stuck, and struggling to find my footing in this new retirement routine.

How long have these adjustment difficulties been going on since they began, and are they still continuing now? Have they lasted more than 6 months after the retirement-related changes and losses settled?

These struggles have been going on for about the last two months and are still continuing now, so they definitely haven't lasted for six months yet. I fully expect these unsettled feelings to fade rather than turn into a long-term problem once I can establish a clearer routine and settle into this retirement rhythm.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began within 3 months of an identifiable psychosocial stressor (retirement, compounded by disruption of planned volunteer/social routines), cause clinically significant distress and impairment beyond expected adjustment, and do not meet criteria for major depressive episode, suicidality, panic disorder, or a longer-standing condition. Duration is under 6 months since onset and the stressor-related changes are ongoing, supporting adjustment disorder.
